Yes. In the current evidence (version 2, knowledge as of 2026-11-12), all four sensors (VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21 and MODIS) covered every day from 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-08. No thermal detections intersected the property in that period.

An earlier version (version 1, dated 2026-10-08) had a gap. It lacked coverage for 7–8 October because the near-real-time data had not yet been published. That version is superseded, and the gap is now filled.

Two caveats. Having no detections doesn't prove that no fire occurred, since small, short, cool or cloud-obscured fires can be missed. The result also says nothing about burned area, cause, or any time outside this period.
